past_cutoff_refuses.error: certificate was issued after its root's distrust cutoff

fix: bind cutoffs from the pins object in exchange
an exception inside the callback that is not a TLSError is now recorded and re-raised instead of being reported as a certificate refusal
notes: a future cutoff leaves the handshake alone; a past cutoff refuses after the chain verifies, which is the intended ordering
the refusal names the cutoff so an operator can tell it apart from a bad chain

offline_evidence_still_valid.config_parsing: root_distrust_after accepts YYMMDDHHMMSSZ and YYYYMMDDHHMMSSZ; rejects bad format, non-SHA256 keys and an empty table
offline_evidence_still_valid.enforcement: a leaf starting after the cutoff is refused; one starting before is allowed; a cutoff for a root the caller does not trust is ignored
offline_evidence_still_valid.table_binding: 1 cutoff entry resolves to an anchor actually present in the 121-certificate bundle

root_cause_of_the_r387_failure.deciding_evidence: r386 (signed off) returned 200 for the identical no-cutoff case in the same environment; r387 failed
root_cause_of_the_r387_failure.description: exchange() never bound a cutoffs name, so the hook raised NameError on every anchored exchange; the error was swallowed and surfaced as a handshake failure
root_cause_of_the_r387_failure.how_it_was_missed_before: the R387 round concluded the new code was innocent because the no-cutoff control also failed — but that round had no r386 control to compare with, so "same error twice" was mistaken for "unrelated"
